summary: Over 14 days of high-quality closed-loop data (98.7% coverage, 5-min cadence), overall time-in-range was 86.0% with average glucose 121.6 mg/dL, but the record includes two clusters of Level-2 hypoglycemia (as low as 41-42 mg/dL) and two clusters of Level-2 hyperglycemia (up to 293 mg/dL), plus a local-time pattern of overnight lows and midday-to-afternoon highs. No carbohydrate entries exist anywhere in the 14-day period, which blocks direct verification of carb ratios, meal-bolus timing, and carb-absorption settings. The currently declared AAPS profile is treated as authoritative for the full period per the user's own declaration, even though telemetry shows repeated Profile Switch events around 2026-08-13 that create some residual uncertainty about continuity. Automation settings (SMB, UAM, Dynamic ISF, safety limits) appear internally consistent, with one notable exception: a basal safety multiplier capped delivery below the algorithm's own requested rate during a severe hyperglycemia episode. No prebolus, immediate-bolus-percentage, or e-carb strategy is declared or observed, so the closed loop is currently handling essentially all meal-related rises reactively through UAM.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is strong (98.7%, 5-min cadence, 0 duplicates/invalid entries, largest gap 65 min). Two edge-of-period partial days exist (Aug 7, Aug 21). Zero carbohydrate entries exist across the whole period despite meal-shaped excursions. profile_context explicitly declares historical_applicability=yes for the current authoritative aaps_profile across the full period, which corrects an earlier working assumption (from checkpoint review) that the Profile Switch events clustered on 2026-08-13T21:23-21:24 necessarily indicate an unknown, different prior configuration for days before that date; per package guidance, historical applicability is a separate user declaration and must not be inferred from telemetry linkage, so that earlier speculation is downgraded to a low-confidence residual observation rather than a firm data gap.

analysis_steps.findings: Aggregate 14-day metrics: average 121.6 mg/dL, SD 39.7, CV 32.6%, TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1% (above a typical <4% target). Level-2 hypoglycemia clusters occurred 2026-08-13 16:59-17:14 (51-42 mg/dL), 2026-08-14 18:04-18:14 (48-41 mg/dL), and an isolated low on 2026-08-21 06:19 (42 mg/dL). Level-2 hyperglycemia clusters occurred 2026-08-15 16:29-16:39 (286-293 mg/dL) and 2026-08-18 11:54-12:14 (285-290 mg/dL). By local hour, hypoglycemia risk peaks overnight/early morning (hour_local 0-3, TBR up to 18.5%), while hyperglycemia risk peaks midday-to-afternoon (hour_local 10-17, TAR up to 32.1% at hour 16). Several therapy_response_windows show glucose continuing to fall for multiple hours after very small correction boluses, consistent with additional automated dosing (SMB) acting after the logged event rather than the bolus alone.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate data to separate meal-driven highs from other causes; cannot confirm SMB continuation after each logged correction bolus from the data provided.

analysis_steps.findings: The overnight/fasting window (hour_local 0-3) has the day's highest TBR (up to 18.5%) even though basal is already at its daily minimum (0.6 U/h at 00:00), arguing against simple basal excess and toward IOB carryover from earlier corrections or the tight 90 mg/dL overnight target. Hours 4-7 local show strong stability (TIR 95.2-98.7%) and are not a concern. The steep hyperglycemia rise at hour_local 9-10 and the peak at hour 16 (avg 162.8 mg/dL, TAR 32.1%) both occur alongside stable or decreasing basal rates (0.8 to 0.7 U/h, then 0.7 to 0.5 U/h), which is inconsistent with basal insufficiency being the primary driver and more consistent with unlogged meals. Hour 19 (basal step-up to 0.7 U/h) shows a secondary TBR peak (15.3%), ambiguous between the rate change and dinner-time correction stacking. Multiple Temporary Targets (135 mg/dL, one 108 mg/dL) overrode profile targets on at least six occasions and are aggregated into the same hourly tables, which limits how cleanly target-segment effects can be isolated.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No isolated basal-only or fasting-test days; no activity/exercise log; Temporary Target windows cannot be excluded from the aggregated hourly averages with the data provided.

analysis_steps.findings: The declared profile uses a single flat ISF segment (56 mg/dL/U), consistent with a deliberately flat-ISF configuration; real-time variable_sens values used by the loop ranged widely (about 27.8 to 178.6 mg/dL/U) because Dynamic ISF (70% adjustment factor) is enabled, which is expected reactive behavior and not itself evidence that the static baseline is wrong. Five carb-ratio segments (13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5, 12.6 g/U) cannot be validated at all because carb_entries=0 and carb_treatment_entries is empty for the entire period; every logged treatment is a Correction Bolus, never a meal bolus. DIA is 10 hours, long relative to typical rapid-acting profiles, and combined with a 25U max IOB ceiling and 3-minute SMB interval, plausibly supports insulin stacking consistent with multi-hour post-correction declines seen in safety_overview; however, the profile name referenced in representative_events ("u200 dilute basal") suggests an extended DIA may be intentional for a diluted insulin concentration, which cannot be confirmed or refuted from this data.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate data (blocks carb-ratio verification entirely); no isolated no-IOB window to test static ISF alone; cannot separate Dynamic ISF correctly reacting to real deviations from partial compensation for an under-strength CR or ISF baseline.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled, consistent with fully closed-loop operation (all sampled statuses show Closed Loop). smb_always_enabled=true means SMB/UAM act regardless of carb state, which matches the observed pattern of COB always at 0 even during clear rises, confirming UAM is doing essentially all meal-response work given zero carb logging. smb_with_temp_target_enabled=true together with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled=false may suppress SMB activity during the several 135 mg/dL Temporary Targets seen in representative_events, a plausible but unconfirmed partial contributor to slower corrections in those windows. SMB delivery settings (3-minute interval, 15/20-minute max SMB/UAM basal minutes) are permissive and, combined with the 10-hour DIA and 25U max IOB, are structurally capable of producing the multi-hour overcorrection-then-drop pattern seen in therapy_response_windows, though the relative contribution of the interval versus DIA cannot be separated from this data.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings; representative_loop_statuses (pump.status=Closed Loop); representative_events Temporary Target entries; therapy_response_windows 2026-08-14, 2026-08-19
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No documentation of AAPS's internal threshold for what counts as a "high" temp target, so the temp-target/SMB-suppression interaction remains a hypothesis; no carb data to confirm UAM is substituting for meal announcements versus reacting to something else.

analysis_steps.findings: max_basal_u_per_hour (12 U/h) and max_iob_units (25 U) were never approached (observed maxima: 4 U/h basal, 5.935 U IOB), so these two settings are not currently binding. A related but separate raw setting, current_basal_safety_multiplier (6x), produced an effective maxSafeBasal of 4 U/h on 2026-08-14T18:40 that capped delivery below the algorithm's own requested rate (about 5.9 U/h) while glucose was rising toward a 256 mg/dL eventual prediction, which is a genuine automation-limit safety observation distinct from a basal-profile defect. autosens_enabled=false while dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true is internally consistent; sensitivity_ratio values near 1 reflect neutral or mildly protective Dynamic ISF output rather than disabled Autosens, and sub-1 values (0.79-0.98) appear in plausible protective contexts (e.g., predicted lows). The wide effective-ISF swings driven by the 70% Dynamic ISF factor cannot be separated, without carb data, from either correct reactive compensation for unlogged meals or partial compensation for an under-strength static CR/ISF baseline.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carb data to separate Dynamic ISF reacting to real unlogged deviations from compensating for a CR/ISF baseline issue; only one clear basal-safety-multiplier capping event is documented in the sampled loop statuses.

analysis_steps.findings: aaps_profile.analysis_context.meal_strategies is an explicit empty array and strategy_stable_for_period is null, meaning no prebolus_minutes or immediate_bolus_percent value is declared for this period; this is treated as a genuine declared absence, not missing data. No meal-bolus events exist in the record at all (every treatment is Correction Bolus or Temp Basal); correction boluses cluster in three loose time bands (overnight/early morning, late-morning/midday, afternoon/evening), and midday/afternoon corrections are frequently given only after glucose is already substantially elevated (e.g., starting values of 141-264 mg/dL), consistent with reactive rather than anticipatory dosing, though this cannot be framed as a deviation from a stated plan since none was declared.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate amount or timing data to confirm which corrections are meal-related; no declared prebolus or bolus-percentage value exists to compare execution against.

analysis_steps.findings: extended_carb_entries=0 and average_extended_carb_duration_min=null confirm e-carbs were not used in this period at all; there is no e-carb amount, start offset, or duration to review, and e-carbs are not treated as equivalent to a pump extended bolus. The carb-absorption settings (min_5m_carbimpact, meal_max_absorption_hours) remain unverifiable for the same reason already noted in profile_cr_isf_dia.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No e-carb or regular-carb entries exist anywhere in the package to support any absorption-timing assessment.

analysis_steps.findings: The clearest safety-priority pattern is recurrent overnight-to-early-morning Level-2 hypoglycemia coinciding with the tightest declared target (90 mg/dL) and the lowest basal rate, confounded by IOB carryover from earlier corrections and by SMB/DIA stacking potential; this is prioritized for observation before any profile change. The clearest data gap blocking multiple stages is the complete absence of carbohydrate logging, which prevents verifying carb ratios, meal-bolus timing, and carb-absorption settings, and also prevents cleanly separating Dynamic ISF's real-time swings from a possible CR/ISF baseline issue. A distinct, resolvable automation-limit finding (the basal safety multiplier capping delivery during the 2026-08-14 severe high) is retained as a separate safety-relevant item, not conflated with the basal profile itself. Per the package's own historical_applicability=yes declaration, the current profile is treated as authoritative for the full 14-day window, lowering confidence in (but not discarding) the earlier hypothesis of a materially different pre-2026-08-13 configuration.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate data; no isolated basal-only or no-IOB test windows; no confirmation of AAPS's internal high-temp-target threshold.

strengths: CGM data quality is excellent across the 14-day period: 98.7% coverage, consistent 5-minute cadence, zero duplicate or invalid entries, and only one gap longer than an hour.
Early morning hours (hour_local 4-7) show strong stability with time-in-range between 95.2% and 98.7% and low time-below-range.
Overall time-in-range across the full period is 86.0%, with all sampled loop statuses showing continuous Closed Loop operation and no evidence of automation dropouts.
Maximum basal (12 U/h) and maximum IOB (25 U) safety ceilings were never approached, indicating those specific limits are not currently constraining therapy.
issues: Recurrent Level-2 hypoglycemia (as low as 41-42 mg/dL) on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and 2026-08-21, with the highest local-hour time-below-range (up to 18.5%) occurring overnight when the declared target is at its tightest (90 mg/dL) and basal at its lowest.

Two clusters of Level-2 hyperglycemia (up to 293 mg/dL) on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18, with a distinct midday-to-afternoon local-hour pattern (time-above-range up to 32.1% at hour 16) that cannot currently be attributed to basal, CR, or ISF because no carbohydrate data exists to separate meal effects.
Zero carbohydrate entries were logged during the entire 14-day period, which blocks verification of all five carb-ratio segments, the carb-absorption settings, and meal-bolus timing.

A basal safety multiplier (6x) produced an effective maxSafeBasal ceiling of about 4 U/h that capped insulin delivery below the algorithm's own requested rate during a severe, worsening hyperglycemia episode on 2026-08-14, independent of the basal profile and the 12 U/h max_basal_u_per_hour limit.

Several therapy_response_windows show glucose continuing to decline for multiple hours after very small named correction boluses, consistent with SMB/UAM continuing to act afterward under a 10-hour DIA, which cannot yet be separated from a possible ISF or CR contribution without carbohydrate data.

implementation_steps: Do not change any profile or AAPS setting yet; begin logging carbohydrate amount and timestamp for meals over at least 5-7 days, prioritizing the 09:00-13:00 and 10:00-17:00 local windows where the largest unexplained swings occur.

Separately, observe and document glucose, IOB, and correction-bolus timing during the 23:00-08:00 window for several nights without concurrent Temporary Target use, to see whether Level-2 lows persist under stable conditions before considering any target or basal change.

Raise the 2026-08-14 basal-safety-multiplier capping event (effective maxSafeBasal about 4 U/h versus an algorithm-requested 5.9 U/h) with a clinician or care team as a distinct automation-limit safety topic, separate from any basal-profile change.
Once carbohydrate data exists, review carb-ratio segments one at a time against actual meal responses, without changing basal, ISF, or DIA at the same time.
Introduce any single profile or AAPS setting change individually, monitor glucose closely for several days afterward, and independently verify the outcome before making the next change.
education: Time-in-range, time-above-range, and time-below-range summarize the share of readings within, above, and below the target glucose band; the 14-day values here (86.0% / 8.9% / 5.1%) provide an overall picture but can hide hour-specific patterns, which is why the hourly local-time breakdown was reviewed separately.

A sensitivity_ratio near 1 in the loop status reflects neutral output from Dynamic ISF/Dynamic sensitivity rather than Autosens being active, since Autosens is disabled in this profile; the larger effective-ISF swings seen in the variable_sens and dosing-sensitivity text come from the separate Dynamic ISF adjustment factor.

Insulin-on-board (IOB) stacking can occur when short SMB intervals, generous per-cycle SMB limits, and a long duration of insulin action (DIA) overlap with repeated correction boluses, which can produce glucose drops many hours after a small logged bolus.

Carbohydrate logging is what allows a closed-loop system's carb ratio, prebolus timing, and e-carb settings to be verified against real glucose responses; without it, glucose rises and falls can only be interpreted as general patterns, not attributed to a specific setting.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only; it does not constitute medical advice and does not modify any AAPS settings automatically.
Any proposed change should be independently verified with a clinician or diabetes care team before being applied.
Change only one setting at a time and monitor glucose closely for several days afterward before making the next change.
Given the recurrent Level-2 hypoglycemia events identified in this data, overnight glucose safety should be discussed and monitored closely before considering any other adjustment.
The basal safety multiplier finding should be reviewed with a care team, since it affected insulin delivery during a severe hyperglycemia episode independently of the basal profile itself.
